title: C1575 — 6R80 transmission assembly connector
introduction:
The round connector gives a useful glimpse of the gearbox's electrical workload: speed, temperature and range information share this reference with sensor supply, returns and solenoid control. I read the function names first to see which job a circuit serves, then follow its cavity and circuit identifiers. Similar wire colors do not make those jobs interchangeable—the gearbox has enough to coordinate without us swapping its name tags.

Keep the transmission identity attached to this reference. Begin with the identification table, use the connector face to find a cavity label, then read the corresponding assignment row across. Repeated rows with different gauge entries remain separate; they are not additional physical cavities, and this page does not choose a gauge for a particular vehicle. The pigtail table is a separate service-parts reference.

This guide explains the map rather than teaching connector access, probing, electrical diagnosis or replacement. Physical viewing direction, test conditions, gauge conventions and the meanings of Size and Used are not established here. Printed abbreviations and bracketed labels remain attached to their functions without guessed expansions or operating specifications.

The summary lists Pin Count 19, while the drawing labels cavities 1–16 and the pigtail row lists 16 cavities. The supplied reference does not reconcile those counts; I do not treat the summary as proof of extra physical positions.

edits.why: I use the circular housing, the long projection toward the drawing's upper left and the inward notch near its lower-left edge as landmarks within the illustration. The cavity labels are distributed around the face rather than arranged as a simple row-by-row grid, so follow the printed labels instead of counting nearby circles. The gray-filled position corresponds to the assignment row with blank circuit and function fields. These observations help connect the picture to the table; the unlabeled housing features do not establish a release mechanism or the physical side from which to view the connector.

Cavity connects a row to the drawing, while Circuit Number keeps that circuit distinct from others with similar colors. Read the remaining fields across the same row. The function descriptions separate shaft-speed, fluid-temperature and transmission-range information from buffered sensor supply, signal returns, solenoid power control and individual solenoid controls. Keep those named roles separate rather than treating a signal return as an interchangeable power connection. Preserve each function's signs, abbreviations and bracketed labels. Where the same cavity and circuit appear with different gauge entries, retain both rows without selecting one or interpreting them as multiple fitted wires. Understanding the row identifies the circuit's documented role; deciding whether it works requires the matching diagnostic procedure.

The pigtail listing brings together the kit identifier, assembly details, service-part reference and engineering-shell reference. I keep the kit's gauge entry separate from the circuit table's gauge entries; this listing does not authorize changing an individual circuit's wire size. The Image field names a referenced illustration rather than showing a lead arrangement here. Use the identifiers for a subsequent applicability check. The listing itself does not teach terminal removal, lead matching, splicing or installation.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata Pin Count differs from the distinct cavity positions shown in the connector face and the pigtail table's cavity total. The assignment table includes repeated gauge entries, but the evidence does not define whether Pin Count counts rows or physical positions. Clarify that field before presenting it as the connector's physical pin total.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all47 primary units, three complete source pages and sole figure, and3 edits. PinCount19 versus pictured1–16/kit16 and repeated gauge assignment ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
